subject: Literature
title: The Brontë Sisters and the Power of Pseudonyms
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Brontë Sisters and the Power of Pseudonyms.

hook.text: Three sisters in a remote Yorkshire parsonage published under male names and changed English literature forever.

buildup.text: Charlotte, Emily, and Anne Brontë became Currer, Ellis, and Acton Bell to be taken seriously in a male-dominated field.

discovery.text: Emily's Wuthering Heights was called 'savage' and 'brutal.' Charlotte's Jane Eyre was an instant sensation.

twist.text: When their identities were revealed, critics who had praised the novels suddenly questioned their quality.

climax.text: The Brontës proved that gender bias in publishing was real and that pseudonyms could subvert it.

punchline.text: They hid behind male names to prove female genius.

quiz.question: How did critics react when the Brontës' real identities were revealed?
options: They celebrated the sisters as groundbreaking women authors
Critics who had praised the novels suddenly questioned their quality
They had already guessed the authors were women
